name: architecture-standards
oneLiner: The estate's architectural constitution: fifteen principles and seventeen guides, also shipped as {{term:plugins|agent plugins}}.
summary: One body of text in two forms. Close to forty-six thousand words of prose in `docs/` (45,893 outside code blocks, 48,664 words in total) is documentation to read **and** the source from which five plugins and twenty-one skills are generated in the {{term:plugins|Agent Plugins 1.0.0}} format. The reason it exists is stated outright: an agent working on another repository is meant to **read** the rules, not reconstruct them from whatever code it happens to see — because that is the most expensive failure in the whole estate. The skills are routers: a short 'use when…' description, a failure-mode table and a checklist, with the full standard sitting alongside and loading only once the skill fires. The generator and the validator are deliberately separate: the first proves the tree agrees with the sources, the second — independently — that a client will accept it. This is the only repository in the portfolio that changes how the rest of the portfolio gets built.
tests: No unit tests. The only automatic verification is the manifest validator (234 lines), which reports '5 plugins, 21 skills, 2 manifests', and the {{term:drift|drift validator}} — and that one fails on HEAD.
ci: Two workflows. `validate-marketplace.yml` runs the generator in `--check` mode and then the validator; the first step exits 1 on HEAD, so **CI is red**. `deploy-pages.yml` publishes the single-page site.

docs.label: The constitution: 15 principles and the compliance checklist

components.name: Konstytucja (P1–P15)
components.description: 667 lines: a diagram of the whole shape of the system, fifteen principles and an eighteen-point compliance checklist. Every principle carries a quoted example from a **working** system — the document is descriptive, not aspirational.

components.name: Seventeen operational guides
components.description: A fixed shape: introduction, numbered sections, failure-mode table, checklist, quoted examples at the end. The largest are deployment to Fly.io (522 lines) and Azure AI Foundry agents (508).

components.name: Standard dokumentacji badawczej
components.description: Defines the layout, the shape of a research document and the evidence rules: every number traceable, reproduction as a command, validate the instrument before trusting its readings, negative results written up as well.

components.name: Generator pakowania
components.description: 363 lines of plain Node. Parses markdown sections while skipping code blocks, trims an excerpt to a 1400-character budget, rewrites links and emits the whole plugin tree. `--check` mode compares the generated tree against the committed one.

components.name: The manifest validator
components.description: 234 lines, deliberately independent of the generator. The generator proves the tree agrees with the sources; the validator proves a client will accept it. That separation is the most important design decision here.

components.name: Wygenerowane drzewo wtyczek
components.description: Five plugins, twenty-one skills. Each has a `plugin.json` at the root **and** in `.claude-plugin/`, because different clients read different paths — a real compatibility problem solved once.

components.name: Propozycje niezmergowane
components.description: Three documents openly marked as not-yet-standard, among them the shared-service extraction pattern with an honest note that it has **one data point**.

overlaps.reason: Cited forty times; the playbook says to adopt it as the single identity provider, and a separate proposal describes its extraction as a pattern.
Cited thirty-one times as the public worked example; part of the standards was extracted from it.
That repository enforces six of these fifteen principles in code. The policy → rule → CI loop is closed.
The reference implementation of the evaluation standard defined here, with a line-by-line account of the deviations and fixes flowing back into the standard.

product: {{term:kernel|Channel and credibility}}, not a transaction. Public, MIT-licensed, and at the same time a real tool that lowers the cost of every agent session over another repository in the estate. The potential commercial consumer is a platform team or a consultant who wants **their own** constitution packaged the same way — at which point what sells is the method (prose plus catalogue plus generator), not the content. The mechanism for distributing it across a whole organisation already exists.
highlights: One body of text, two forms: 45,893 words of prose outside code blocks (48,664 words in total across `docs/**/*.md`) are documentation and the source of five plugins at once — without a single line copied by hand.

A real client-compatibility problem solved: Copilot reads `plugin.json` at the root, Claude Code reads it in `.claude-plugin/`, and agents want the `.agent.md` extension in one place and plain `.md` in the other. The generator emits both spellings, the validator keeps the manifests from diverging.
Private repositories are cited under stable placeholders with a legend — the example shows the shape without disclosing the source.
The skills are routers, not the standard pasted into the prompt: the full text loads only once the skill fires. That is the difference between a hundred tokens and a thousand on every session.
gaps: **CI is red on HEAD.** One commit changed a source document without regenerating the tree, so the {{term:drift|drift validator}} exits with an error. A repository whose central claim is 'no copy-paste drift' is drifting — and that is the best possible evidence the mechanism works.

MARKETPLACE.md says three skills where there are four, and twenty where there are twenty-one. The table is written by hand — which is exactly the problem the generator already solved for the plugin tree.
All the plugins have version 1.0.0 hard-coded from the start, and the marketplace is served from the default branch — a consumer has no way to detect that the contents changed.
No tests for the generator. The only verification that the markdown parser works is that its output matches the committed tree.
The token-cost figures are given as measured, but the repository holds neither a script nor a record of the measurement — contradicting its own research-standard rule on reproducibility.
next: Run the generator and commit the regenerated tree so CI goes green again. It is one command and it is first on the list for the whole portfolio.
Generate the skills table in MARKETPLACE.md from the catalogue instead of writing it by hand.
Add a check to the validator that every reference to a principle has a matching heading in the constitution.
Introduce release tagging for the marketplace — today every merge to the default branch immediately changes what everyone installing gets.
Record the token-cost measurement method as a command, or remove the figures, in line with your own rule.
risks: The generated tree has diverged from the source on HEAD — that is not only red CI but a real risk that somebody installs a skill carrying an older version of the standard than the documentation.
No release versioning, with manifests declaring 1.0.0 from the start.
The redaction of private repository names covers HEAD; your own guide on open-source release calls for an audit of the **history**, not just the current state.
headline: The drift validator is red — the repository about not drifting is drifting
